summary:
**Mission Control 3D** is an interactive educational game that allows users to design, plan, and simulate a space mission. Players choose a mission objective, spacecraft, scientific instruments, communication system, launch vehicle, and orbital trajectory while balancing important engineering factors such as mass, power, budget, science, reliability, data return, and mission risk.

The game guides players through a mission timeline from launch and orbit or transfer to science operations, data transmission, and mission completion. It also provides a visual representation of the spacecraft, destination, and trajectory to help users understand the spatial relationships involved in space missions.

The project is designed to make complex aerospace engineering concepts easier and more engaging for students, beginners, and space enthusiasts. By turning mission planning into an interactive game, users can experiment with different designs, understand engineering trade-offs, learn from mission failures, and improve their final mission.

**Live Demo:** https://rainbow-centaur-aea5cf.netlify.app
details:
Project Title

Mission Control 3D: Design, Plan, and Simulate a Space Mission

Live Project

Play Mission Control 3D

Project Type

Interactive educational space mission design and simulation game

Project Idea

Mission Control 3D is an interactive game that teaches users how real space missions are planned. The player acts as a mission designer and makes engineering decisions about the spacecraft, scientific instruments, communications, launch vehicle, orbital trajectory, and mission timeline.

The player must balance competing factors such as:

  • ⚖️ Mass
  • 🔋 Power
  • 💰 Budget
  • 🔬 Science value
  • 📡 Communication
  • 🛡️ Reliability
  • ⚠️ Mission risk
  • 📊 Data return

The goal is to create a mission that successfully reaches its destination and completes its scientific objectives.

Main Features

1. Mission Concept

The player chooses a mission such as:

  • Earth Observation
  • Weather Monitoring
  • Lunar Mapping
  • Mars Exploration

2. Spacecraft Design

The player selects a spacecraft platform and scientific instruments.

3. Orbital Trajectory

The player can choose different mission trajectories, including:

  • Low Earth Orbit
  • Polar/Sun-Synchronous Orbit
  • Geostationary Orbit
  • Earth–Moon Transfer
  • Lunar Orbit
  • Mars Transfer

4. Mission Timeline

The simulation follows important mission events such as:

Launch → Orbit/Transfer → Cruise → Arrival → Science Operations → Data Transmission → Mission Completion

5. Space Visualization

The game visually shows the spacecraft, destination and trajectory so users can understand the spatial relationship between them.

6. Engineering Trade-offs

Every decision affects the mission. For example, a more powerful instrument may increase science value but also increase mass, power consumption and cost.

7. Mission Simulation

After completing the design, the player launches the mission and watches its progress through different mission phases.

8. Final Mission Evaluation

At the end, the game calculates a mission score based on factors such as:

  • Science
  • Reliability
  • Risk
  • Budget
  • Power
  • Data return
  • Mission success

The player also receives an engineering lesson explaining what worked or what caused problems.
